history.method: Normalized Unicode/case/alphanumeric comparison on all files in the base commit evidence tree, decompressing gzip and reading tar members, plus the early catalogue. Identifiers and title aliases above.

companion.locator: Section II.A and Figure 1 (test rig), II and III (observer and scenarios).

grade: Physical single-joint-equivalent 185:1 Nabtesco cycloidal rig. Three distinct PT100 channels measure lubricant (refill port), housing and environment. Load-side motor is commanded to 0 Nm. No raw pre/post-clamp commands. The provided column tau_f is labeled friction torque; its per-row measurement/construction chain is not documented in the data. The companion describes a modeled friction torque driven by velocity and lubricant temperature in the observer. Do not equate this column to a separately measured output-shaft torque.
scope: Every released original source, 13 measurements and 2 MATLAB helpers verified against original-format publisher MD5. 7,937,638 rows across files, including duplicate acquisition intervals. All six numeric columns finite, timestamps increase; nominal sample spacings of 2.5, 25 or 100 milliseconds, depending on the file. Differences are not estimated by pooling rows across frequencies.
contrast: Five constant-speed identification datasets: restrict signed speed to the corresponding measured direction within 2% of file nominal magnitude. In each file compare stored abs(tau_f) medians at measured lubricant T_L in [22,24) and [44,46) °C. All five decrease; drops range 1.5963–3.1458 Nm. The slowest identification file is consistently negative despite an unsigned name. Temperatures vary during each run; observations are serially dependent. This summarizes the published channel conditional on speed, not an independent verification of a friction law.
overlap: Both 86,401-row 36 minute heat-up validation files at 0.6283 and 1.2566 rad/s are exact numerical six-column prefixes of their corresponding 576,001-row, 4 h long-term validation files. These intervals must not be counted as independent repetitions. This test does not claim a complete all-subsequence de-duplication across every file.
reproduce: Python 3 + pandas + NumPy. Download each original file using the URL and relative path in inputs. Run python derive_thermal.py SOURCE OUT. Three CSVs cover per-file temperature and time, within-record temperature bands, and exact prefix checks.
